results.explanation: At the declared handler entry, the source first establishes the authenticated caller through requireCurrentSpaceUser (lines 742-745), then binds the requested target and the caller's membership in the selected space through resolveSpaceMemberResource (lines 746-748; binding details at lines 632-662). Under the accepted premise that the target is a different active member in the same space and resolution succeeds, targetUser.ID differs from currentUser.ID, so the non-self branch is taken (lines 750-751). That branch requires the caller membership to be an administrator; requireSpaceAdministrator rejects a non-administrator with PermissionDenied (lines 54-58), and the supplied principal is an active ordinary non-administrator. Therefore the source-visible authorization result is deny before the protected DeleteSpaceMember store effect at lines 756-760. Separately, the accepted policy allows an active member to remove a different active member of the same space without administrator authority, so the policy result is allow. The source-visible denial therefore conflicts with the accepted policy for this scenario. No decisive source-external fact is required within the declared-entry boundary because the accepted premises fix the target relation, successful resource resolution, and non-administrator role; source discovery remains not-tested.
